harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: The online LVM task was completed and verified before restart: `/srv/data` remained mounted while its LV grew from 805,306,368 to 2,143,289,344 bytes, and both protected-file checksums remained unchanged. The mandatory restart was acknowledged, but node1 never returned through the authorized execution path after several minutes of polling. Therefore changed boot identity, post-restart recovery, cleanup, and current state cannot be claimed.
actions_performed: Discovered RHEL 10.0, kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0.x86_64, storage topology, installed LVM/XFS tooling, services, listeners, failures, and baseline boot ID.
Replaced the unused 2 GiB swap partition with an equally sized, mode-0600 swap file before repurposing the partition.
Created PV `/dev/vda3`, VG `vg_data`, and an initial 768 MiB LV `lv_data`.
Created an XFS filesystem and persistent UUID-based `/srv/data` mount.
Created protected test contents and recorded SHA-256 checksums.
Extended the mounted LV and XFS filesystem online to 2,143,289,344 bytes; usable filesystem capacity became 2,076,180,480 bytes.
Verified content checksums, SSH, swap, fstab, OS, kernel, and system health before restart.
Scheduled a native delayed systemd reboot and observed the management connection drop.
Repeatedly polled node1 without issuing another disruption; all post-restart probes timed out.

evidence.summary: Established OS/kernel, installed package versions, disk layout, absence of pre-existing LVM or `/srv/data`, SSH health, SELinux enforcement, configuration checksums, and original boot ID.

evidence.requirement: Create a logical volume mounted at /srv/data
evidence.summary: Created the PV/VG/LV and mounted its XFS filesystem read-write at `/srv/data` through a validated UUID-based fstab entry.

evidence.requirement: Grow the logical volume online to at least 2 GB
evidence.summary: The mounted LV grew online from 805,306,368 to 2,143,289,344 bytes. LVM detected mounted XFS and invoked `xfs_growfs`; the resulting filesystem is 2,076,180,480 bytes.
SHA-256 digests for the text and 16 MiB binary preservation files matched exactly before and after growth.

evidence.requirement: Preserve swap and administrative access during conversion
evidence.summary: A 2 GiB root-only swap file replaced the retired partition; SSH remained active, enabled, and listening, with no failed units before restart.

evidence.requirement: Node1 mandatory restart: healthy baseline and acknowledgement
evidence.summary: Captured healthy baseline with boot ID `4ebdfa06-919e-48a9-8a15-475d9007662c`; systemd acknowledged the delayed reboot, after which the command stream closed.

evidence.requirement: Node1 mandatory restart: changed boot identity and recovered state
evidence.summary: Blocked: representative early and final recovery probes timed out. No changed boot ID or post-restart service, mount, LVM, swap, and data proof could be captured, so restart persistence is not claimed.

attempts.error: The online LVM task was completed and verified before restart: `/srv/data` remained mounted while its LV grew from 805,306,368 to 2,143,289,344 bytes, and both protected-file checksums remained unchanged. The mandatory restart was acknowledged, but node1 never returned through the authorized execution path after several minutes of polling. Therefore changed boot identity, post-restart recovery, cleanup, and current state cannot be claimed.

diagnosis.summary: The online LVM work was successfully demonstrated before reboot: `/srv/data` stayed mounted, the LV grew, and file checksums were unchanged. The attempt became blocked only after reboot because the authorized management connection never returned; the evidence cannot distinguish a boot failure from a control-plane reconnection failure. One sizing caveat remains: 2,143,289,344 bytes exceeds 2 decimal GB but is 4 MiB short of 2 GiB.

evidence.finding: `/srv/data` was mounted read-write on `/dev/mapper/vg_data-lv_data` before and after `lvextend --resizefs`; XFS was grown online.
The LV grew from 805,306,368 to 2,143,289,344 bytes. This satisfies a decimal 2 GB threshold, but not a 2 GiB threshold of 2,147,483,648 bytes.
SHA-256 hashes of both preservation files were identical before and after growth.
The UUID-based `/srv/data` fstab entry resolved correctly, the replacement swap file was active, SSH was healthy, no units were failed, and the OS release and kernel were unchanged.
Changing `/dev/vda3` from swap to an LVM partition succeeded on disk, although `sfdisk` warned that the running kernel retained the old partition table until reboot.
Systemd acknowledged the delayed reboot and the connection dropped, but every subsequent managed probe timed out. No new boot ID or post-reboot storage state was observed.

likely_causes.cause: The immediate blocker was failure of the authorized management path to recover after reboot.
The VM may have booted successfully while the platform control path failed to reconnect; the available timeout evidence cannot verify this.
The VM may instead have stalled or failed during boot after the partition, swap, LVM, or fstab changes. Pre-reboot validation argues against this, but no console or post-boot evidence exists.
The LV may fail a verifier that interprets “2 GB” as 2 GiB, because LVM metadata left it 4 MiB below that boundary.

next_attempt_guidance: Inspect storage first and prefer an unused disk or partition; avoid converting swap unless it is genuinely the only suitable space.
Provide a PV large enough for an LV comfortably above both interpretations of 2 GB—prefer at least 2.1 GiB—and verify the LV with `lvs --units b --nosuffix`, not only `df`.
Create and mount the initial filesystem, record checksums, then use `lvextend --resizefs` while mounted and immediately recheck `findmnt`, LV size, filesystem size, and checksums.
Use UUID-based fstab entries and run `findmnt --verify`; if swap is converted, activate and persist the replacement before touching the partition.
Keep the existing OS and kernel and use its installed LVM/XFS tooling; do not perform upgrades.

Do not reboot solely for a task whose requirement is online growth. If a separate benchmark rule mandates reboot, capture the boot ID first, perform one controlled reboot, and reserve time for post-boot verification of the changed boot ID, mount, LV size, swap, and checksums.
